title: Free variables removed when processing a clause
statement:
Let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables, and write $f(\rho)$ for the number of free variables of a restriction $\rho$. Present a single clause as a list of $k$ literals, each paired with its position index, and a decision-tree path as a list of $m$ variable–direction pairs. Suppose that every literal's variable is free in $\rho_0$ and that the listed literals have pairwise distinct variables. Let $\rho_0'$ be the updated restriction returned in place of $\rho_0$ when these literals are processed against the path. Then
\[
f(\rho_0') + \min(k, m) = f(\rho_0),
\]
so processing fixes exactly $\min(k, m)$ of the previously free variables of $\rho_0$.
